Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: preserve its warm coastal rice-field setting, people’s modest 1970s rural clothes, family character identities, muted ochre and grey-blue colors, and watercolor texture. Its tractor/trailer migration vehicle is factually wrong and must be fully replaced, and its walking family should now be shown taking the truck.

Image 3 is the approved watercolor portrait of that same man, for face geometry and painted style.

Scene and composition: one wide complete painting, a departure pause on a level rural road in a low coastal farming landscape. The MAIN moving truck is stationary while the family is settled for the journey, with all wheels grounded and natural perspective. Use a simple late-1960s/1970s style modest bonneted cargo truck, round headlights, weathered grey-blue body, dark tires and an ordinary high-sided wooden or metal cargo bed, no identifiable brand or precise model. View it at three-quarter side angle so its cab, loaded cargo bed and family remain clearly readable. Bae, wearing his established cap and ordinary grey-blue work jacket, is a PASSENGER at the camera-side cab window, visible head and upper body. He is not touching a steering wheel. Do not identify or feature the driver; the far-side driver area is naturally obscured. His expression is calm, thoughtful, quietly resolute. Preserve his real broad midface and cheeks, softly hooded narrow eyes, familiar brows, broad rounded nose, lip shape, rounded jaw, ears and black hairline, with slightly fewer age lines for age about 45. Integrate the face into the painting; never paste a photograph or substitute a generic farmer.
The elderly mother, wife and two children from the original scene retain their distinct appearances and clothes and are shown seated low inside the enclosed high-sided rear cargo bed, safely away from the truck's edges and wheels, visibly associated with the move. There is a clear low seated passenger area separate from secured household bundles; no one standing or sitting on the rim, climbing, dangling limbs, or walking in wheel paths. The truck is paused, with no dust plume or speed effect. Tie modest bedding bundles, household baskets and compact farming equipment down securely below the rail. Farm equipment, if visible, is cargo only, never the towing vehicle. Behind the main truck, softly painted smaller moving trucks with household bundles suggest the neighboring seven-household migration, without making a factual claim about an exact number of vehicles. No crowds added to the foreground. Preserve low fields, distant blue coastal water and hazy hills as soft contextual washes, without claiming a specific route or landmark.

Style: paint EVERY surface in the existing series' hand-painted watercolor on warm cold-pressed paper, transparent ochre and restrained grey-blue washes, visible pigment blooms and granulation, broad brush-shaped marks, soft wet-on-wet transitions, light paper highlights and lost edges with selective clear strokes for faces and essential truck details. No photograph with a uniform speckled paint filter, pasted face, glossy skin, hyper-detailed digital rendering, oil impasto, cartoon or hard outlines.
Framing: landscape, preferably exact 16:9, essential truck, Bae's face and family within a generous central safe area so a centered 16:9 crop preserves them. Leave some rural landscape margin around the scene; truck and family must be large enough to read on a phone.
Avoid: the old walking tractor or tow trailer as transport, boats, people walking as the principal means of the journey, a smiling advertisement, unsafe riding or traffic action, modern trucks or cars, luxury factory, exact branded truck identity, readable license plate, signage, lettering, text, caption, logo, watermark, decorative border, panels or collage. Opaque background.
